rawBridgePoolLifetime.previousDefect: Long-lived DataVault TryLockBuffer pins were used to protect native-exported bridge pointers, but those pins can block arena relocation/growth while the audio bridge is active.
rawBridgePoolLifetime.failureMode: If any raw bridge allocation fails, Initialize disposes and descriptor registration stays fail-closed. C# bridge validation re-reads SharedState capacity/mask/guards/source-channel metadata before P/Invoke and returns SharedStateInvalid if it no longer matches the descriptor/native contract. SourceChannels is copied into the immutable descriptor at NativeAudioFrameRingBuffer.cs:431, and native callback reads ringBuffer.sourceChannels at Plugin_HectonSensoryKernel.cpp:440 instead of trusting mutable SharedState for frame stride. TryClear rejects native Active or Busy status. If native clear fails for any status except PluginUnavailable while H8Memory is initialized, raw buffers are retained and reinitialize is blocked before any second allocation. If H8Memory is already shut down, raw pointers are nulled instead of retained because their backing memory has already been reaped, and TryResolveRingViews refuses to create NativeArray views over those stale addresses. If managed shared-state cursors are corrupt, TryReadSharedFrameIndex rejects raw indices outside [0, capacityFrames) instead of masking them through capacityMask; producer/DSP bookkeeping records TelemetryStatusSharedStateInvalid and triggers the dump route. Hot telemetry writes go to a stable H8Memory raw 300-entry ring and do not acquire a DataVault writer fence or call Thread.MemoryBarrier. The writer marks a slot Sequence=0 before field writes, publishes final non-zero Sequence last with Volatile.Write, and dump/mirror readers validate sequence plus StateHash through TryReadTelemetryEntryStable before copying a DTO. Fault/shutdown paths best-effort mirror the raw ring into BufferID.AudioFrameRingTelemetry with TryAcquireWriteLock; if the mirror lock is unavailable, the raw binary dump still proceeds and the writer does not block. Native dump export queues the fixed snapshot into a static native scratch buffer and returns without inline fwrite/fopen; if the queue is busy, bad, or thread creation fails, native returns 0 and C# resets the dump gate so the next fault can retry. Final disk write success after queueing remains runtime validation debt.
